unclear.text: Does K3(c) cover a paid notice period of six to twelve months in which the worker may not work for anyone else?
readings: U1-a: yes, any paid notice period in which the worker remains employed is preserved
U1-b: no, a notice period long enough to keep the worker out of the field is a restraint in effect and void under K1

unclear.text: Is a term requiring a worker who leaves within 24 months to repay employer-paid training a penalty under K1?
readings: U2-a: yes, it penalizes leaving, and leaving is how one comes to work for another
U2-b: no, it applies to every departure and only recovers a cost

a1.text: Non-competes deter some bound workers from moves to rivals or start-ups they would otherwise make.

a2.text: Employers stop enforcing, and workers learn that the clause is void (K4 notices, damages and fee-shifting).

a5.text: In a material share of trainee jobs, the non-compete protected the employer's recovery of the cost of general training.

a7.text: Some bound workers are paid less than a rival would pay them.

a18.text: The Labor Bureau's budget is not raised for the new task.

a26.text: In the counterfactual, some Teravel employment contracts contain paid notice periods of six months or more, and some contain training repayment agreements.

a28.text: In the counterfactual, firms that hire a bound worker from a rival bear litigation risk, demand letters or buy-out payments.

a29.text: Some existing contracts contain forfeiture-for-competition clauses (deferred pay lost only on joining a competitor).

n1.text: Employers and workers expect the Act to take effect on 1 January 2026 once it has passed.
